subject: Trial path decision capture — hosted vs dedicated vs private
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam@vitalpay.com>, Priya Rao <priya.rao@vitalpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Sep 2028 17:08:00 -0700
Subject: Trial path decision capture — hosted vs dedicated vs private

Hi Sam / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the demo today — appreciated the honest feedback and the product use cases you walked through. I wanted to capture the decision points we discussed so we can move toward a sponsored pilot quickly and avoid back-and-forth. Please reply inline with any clarifications.

Summary from our side (high level):
- Current preference: evaluate Hosted API first to accelerate time-to-value; Dedicated or Private only if we hit data residency or regulatory blocking items.
- Key constraints you mentioned: SOC 2 evidence, 90-day logs, ability to rotate keys, and a single-VPC peering path if we escalate to Private.
- Performance targets: you said ~80 RPS spiky (up to 120 RPS for short bursts) for the fraud-check endpoint; average ~10 RPS for background scoring. Latency SLO target: p95 < 300ms for the user-facing path.
- Integration notes: embedding store will be in your AWS account; we need to confirm egress cost expectations and whether a webhook-based callback model is acceptable.

Open questions for you (please confirm):
1) Data residency: do you require EU-only hosting (would push toward Private/VPC) or is US-hosted acceptable for the pilot?
2) PII: will the payloads include cardholder data or other regulated PII that must never leave your VPC?
3) Pilot traffic: can you share an estimated test load (RPS + tokens per request) and an expected test duration (2 weeks recommended)?
4) Security paperwork: we can provide SOC2 artifacts and an SCP for sandbox log access — any specific evidence you need beyond SOC2 and a security questionnaire?

Next steps we propose from Redwood:
- Provide a two-week Hosted pilot (sandbox endpoint + a single canary staging endpoint) with token-limited ratecaps that match your test load.
- Share a lightweight SOW and ratecard (attached) so procurement can review.
- Kick off a short security handoff call with our security engineer if you confirm SOC2 + 90d logs are sufficient.

Attachments: vitalpay-sow-draft.pdf (SOW draft), ratecard_v3.xlsx (pilot pricing bands). Canary plan template link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1ExampleCanaryTemplate

If Hosted looks good on the pilot we'll draft a runbook for Dedicated/Private requirements and what migration would look like.

Can you please reply with answers to Q1–Q4 and a preferred pilot start week (we have openings the weeks of 9/25 and 10/9)?

Thanks —
Irene

Irene — thanks for the recap and succinct ask. Replying inline below.

> 1) Data residency: do you require EU-only hosting (would push toward Private/VPC) or is US-hosted acceptable for the pilot?
US-hosted is fine for the pilot. If the pilot goes to prod, we may need multi-region (US + EU) depending on customer expansion, but that's a later conversation.

> 2) PII: will the payloads include cardholder data or other regulated PII that must never leave your VPC?
No CHD in payloads for the pilot. We will scrub or tokenise anything regulated. There will be some user identifiers and partial account numbers for debugging, which we can hash.

> 3) Pilot traffic: can you share an estimated test load (RPS + tokens per request) and an expected test duration (2 weeks recommended)?
Estimate: baseline 8 RPS, expected surge up to 80 RPS for peak windows, short bursts to 120 RPS for <30s. Avg tokens/request ~1,200 (reason: context + short doc). We'll aim for the two-week pilot starting 2028-09-25.

> 4) Security paperwork: we can provide SOC2 artifacts and an SCP for sandbox log access — any specific evidence you need beyond SOC2 and a security questionnaire?
SOC2 + 90-day logs + proof of key rotation policy should be sufficient for Legal & Security to greenlight the pilot. If you have an ISV-hosted SOC supplement or a privacy/dataflow diagram, send that too and we'll loop Legal.

Attaching our internal security checklist (security_qs.pdf) to this reply.

Sam

Thanks Sam — clear and helpful. Looping from our side with a concrete quickstart/canary plan so procurement/security can see an operational path.

Proposed Hosted pilot plan (2 weeks) — key pieces:
- Endpoints:
  * sandbox.redwood/vitalpay/chat -> chat/generation endpoint (auth: API key)
  * sandbox.redwood/vitalpay/score -> low-latency scoring endpoint for fraud-check (same model, lower timeout)
- Rate limits for pilot:
  * baseline throttle: 10 RPS sustained (to match dev traffic)
  * pilot burst cap: 120 RPS windowed to 30s (we'll protect other tenants)
  * token cap: 250k tokens/min account-wide during pilot (we can refine based on your avg token/request)
- Observability: p95 latency, token consumption, per-key breakdown in Console. We will grant VitalPay a read-only Console link scoped to the sandbox project.
- Security & logs: 90-day request logs exported to an S3 bucket (read-only role to be provided by VitalPay) + SOC2 package attached. Key rotation: support for customer-side key rotation via API.
- Rollout criteria: proceed to production Dedicated or Private if either:
  1) Legal disallows hosted model for prod, or
  2) sustained average > 60 RPS for 24h and economics favor a reserved pool.

Operational next steps (action items):
1) VitalPay: confirm start date (Sam proposed 2028-09-25) and share AWS role for logs + security_qs.pdf (attached).
2) Redwood: finalize SOW (vitalpay-sow-draft.pdf), send DocuSign link for signature, provision sandbox endpoints and invite your engineers to the Console.
3) Schedule 30-minute security handoff the week prior to start (we're proposing 9/22 or 9/23).

If the above aligns we'll update the SOW with the pilot ratecaps and a short acceptance checklist. Marissa will be the engagement lead on provisioning; copying her so she can start tickets.

Ben
